question: What fish evidence does the 2013 Bolinao MPA study report, and what remains unresolved before its findings could support a public species record?

method.summary: Reviewed the Silliman Journal article landing page, the publisher-hosted full-text PDF (methods and fish results), the Vol. 54 No. 1 issue record, and the journal copyright policy. The PDF is available from the publisher. No local copy, full table transcription, photograph, figure, or extracted dataset was retained.
method.bibliographicDateFinding: The issue and PDF identify Silliman Journal Vol. 54 No. 1, January–June 2013. The migrated article landing page displays Published 2022-10-06; this is recorded separately and is not treated as the original issue date.
method.surveyFinding: The methods state that the survey was conducted in November–December 2009 in four coastal barangays of Bolinao: Arnedo, Balingasay, Binabalian, and Victory. Three stations were established per barangay in coralline MPA areas. Fish were surveyed by snorkeling visual census using ten 10 m by 5 m quadrats per station; divers waited one minute after deploying each quadrat, recorded and counted visible fish, and took underwater photographs to help verify identification. The article says site locations were determined with GPS but the reviewed text provides no machine-readable station coordinates or datum. Species identifications cite LGU references, FishBase, and local residents; voucher specimens or accessions are not reported in the reviewed methods/results.
method.rightsFinding: The Silliman Journal copyright page says article copyright is held by the journal and individual authors and describes permission requirements for reproducing full articles, long quotations, or multiple tables/figures. No Creative Commons or item-specific data-reuse license was found for this article. The fish table, images, and map were not reproduced; publication or public-app reuse approval remains false.

studyAreaLead.sourceNameAsReported: Marine protected areas in the coastal barangays of Arnedo, Balingasay, Binabalian, and Victory
studyAreaLead.habitatLane: marine coastal / coralline MPA areas; no exact station-to-waterbody crosswalk

publication.title: Assessment of Marine Protected Areas in Four Coastal Barangays of Bolinao, Pangasinan
publication.citation: Paz-Alberto, A. M., & Teñoso, A. R. D. (2013). Assessment of Marine Protected Areas in Four Coastal Barangays of Bolinao, Pangasinan. Silliman Journal, 54(1).
publication.accessStatus: Publisher landing page, issue page, full-text PDF, and journal copyright policy reviewed online on 2026-11-19.
publication.license: No open license or item-specific data-reuse grant verified. The journal copyright page states published article copyright is held by the journal and individual authors.

internalConsistency.issue: The abstract and parts of the results print Chlororus microrhinos, while the fish table prints Chlorurus microrhinos.
internalConsistency.disposition: Preserve the abstract-reported label in this source screen; do not silently normalize or assert identity. A separate nomenclatural check would only identify candidate name strings, not the sampled fish.

internalConsistency.issue: The fish table prints Cheilinus trilobatus, while the results prose and importance-value table print Cheilinus tribatus.
internalConsistency.disposition: Record the conflict as unresolved and retain no merged taxon or occurrence row.

internalConsistency.issue: The fish table prints Arothron hispidus, while the importance-value table prints Arothon hispidus; other prose also contains additional name spelling variants.
internalConsistency.disposition: Do not treat the table/prose strings as independently verified specimen identifications.

internalConsistency.issue: The publisher landing page shows a 2022 publication date even though the journal issue and PDF identify Vol. 54 No. 1, January–June 2013.
internalConsistency.disposition: Record the original issue period and migrated-page date separately.

interpretation: This is a useful historical primary-source lead for marine fish research in four named Pangasinan coastal barangays. It is one 2009 visual-census snapshot, not a complete checklist for Bolinao, Pangasinan, or Region I, and it does not establish present-day occurrence or catch probability.
The methods report GPS use but provide no machine-readable station coordinates or datum in the reviewed text. Do not infer a point, MPA polygon, boundary, or navigation geometry from the figures.
The article's historical description of MPA/no-take management is not current legal advice, proof of present boundaries, or evidence of fishing access, rules, or water safety.

Taxon spellings conflict between the abstract, fish table, and results tables; vouchers/accessions are not reported. The reported counts and high-importance labels remain source claims and are not normalized species assertions.

No article table, map, photograph, raw dataset, species assertion, occurrence record, geometry, photo, legal recommendation, or public-app row was added. The journal's copyright policy was reviewed, but no item-specific license or permission was established. Region I and Luzon remain incomplete.

decision.reason: The full paper provides a dated, named-site visual-census lead, but table/prose name variants, absent vouchers and coordinates, historical-only scope, and unverified reuse rights prevent app-facing admission.

nextAction: If this source is needed for public species evidence, first perform a bounded source-string crosscheck without merging the conflicting labels, verify whether author or publisher permission is required for a derived checklist, and seek station metadata or an independently reusable source with locality-level sampling records. Continue the Region I source sweep across marine, estuarine, brackish, and inland waterbodies.
